comment: ps-move's feature answers in lane DD-2's answer-table form (FeatureStubSpec), prepared for that table to take once it merges. Each byte comes from a cited capture or layout. capture_fidelity_check (S96) checks these bytes against the moveonpc wiki and decodes the calibration as psmoveapi does. The 0x10 entry needs one thing DD-2's form does not have yet: pages on a plain entry, served to successive GETs in turn and wrapping to the first, the counter kept for the device's lifetime, as a real Move answers 0x10 (Calibration data: it has to be read three times, and the first block read may be any of the three). The ZCM2 Move answers its two blocks the same way (Calibration-data-CECH-ZCM2, lines 8 and 38).

reports.comment: Bluetooth addresses, 16 bytes with the ID (the descriptor's 0x0F data bytes). The controller's own address backwards from byte 1, 08 25 00 at 7 to 9, the host's address backwards from byte 10 (moveonpc HID reports, lines 9-11 at 033ab8e: 04 66 55 44 33 22 11 08 25 00 FF EE DD CC BB AA). psmoveapi reads the controller's address as a USB Move's serial (psmove.c:560-570, 935-962 at 97d97e9). The address is 02:48:4D:00:00:<index>, locally administered as the DualSense model's pairing MAC is, so it cannot collide with a real controller's. The host address is zeros: no source gives the address of a Move that was never paired.

Calibration, three 49-byte blocks with indices 00, 01 and 82, the sample at the top of moveonpc Calibration data (lines 10-25 at 033ab8e), which reassembled is the second of the page's eight dumps. psmoveapi reads 0x10 three times and places each block by its index (psmove.c:974-1022), RPCS3 reads two and places them by index (ps_move_handler.cpp:292-325 at c82221f): with the counter kept across hosts, a second RPCS3 connect gets 0x82 and 00, as it would from a real Move. ps-move's motion scale and zero come from these blocks, read as psmoveapi reads them, so a host that calibrates from them reads the profile's motion back in g and degrees per second.
